Mitosis is an equational division of a somatic cell where one parent cell divides into two daughter cells, each having the same chromosome number and genetic constitution as the parent ($2n$). In contrast, meiosis is a reductional division resulting in four daughter cells, each with half the chromosome number of the parent cell ($n$).
